questions: Does the starting block count as a path (the zero-move path)?

Are paths considered distinct if they visit the same sequence of blocks but in a different order? Since moves are only positive x or positive y, order is determined by sequence of blocks, but clarification needed on whether different sequences of the same blocks are possible.
Is the starting block chosen uniformly from all blocks, or do we count all possible (start, path) pairs?
Do we count paths that end at any block, or only paths that cannot be extended further?
Are blocks at (x,y) with L ≤ x ≤ R and D ≤ y ≤ U the only ones existing, or do the inequalities define a rectangular region within 0..W and 0..H?
If a path goes from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2), must every intermediate lattice point on the straight line segment be a block, or only the actually visited lattice points?
Should the answer be computed modulo 998244353 at the end, or should intermediate calculations also be taken modulo?
Are the constraints L,R,D,U actually used? The clarification says blocks exist at all (x,y) with 0≤x≤W, 0≤y≤H, making L,R,D,U seemingly irrelevant.
